credentialSupplyDuringFutureApprovedExec: Owner privately selects an approved source only after authority, logging, custody and execution prerequisites pass; no source is selected by this review.

In the separately approved isolated local Node process, readA02AdminCredentials uses the dedicated hidden TTY for two opaque inputs: API-key field and raw bearer-token field. No environment/argv/file secret source is used.

The returned disposable provider is supplied directly as adminHeaderProvider to createA02AuthCreator. The existing transport sends only to the pinned Development route; raw payload/header serialization is intentional at the wire boundary and must not be logged.
Dispose providers in finally and terminate the protected process. This releases retained references, not guaranteed zeroization of previous copies or operating-system buffers.

capabilityMetadata.installedSdkContract: Local SDK documents server-only Admin create/delete contracts and required privileged credentials; it does not attest any particular source or actual credential.
capabilityMetadata.metadataLimit: No supported, independently authoritative credential-capability proof is established in the existing local package without provider evidence. This is not a claim that Supabase has no metadata interface; no live interface was inspected or invented.
capabilityMetadata.sourceCustodyLimit: Even source/type capability metadata cannot prove which bytes are later entered, their present validity or successful Gateway acceptance. Custody and actual approved execution remain separate.
capabilityMetadata.postgresAuthorityLimit: Historical PostgreSQL role/cleanup privileges do not establish HTTP Auth Admin credential authority.

findings.scope: Source-code architecture and synthetic tests only
findings.facts: Explicit operator hidden-TTY input produces a disposable in-memory Admin header provider; imports are inert. There is no credential-source lookup or automatic discovery.

findings.scope: Static destination and input project label only
findings.facts: The Admin transport fixes the exact Development HTTPS host, POST route, TLS hostname and nominated IDs, rejecting alternate URLs/methods. The provider requires the exact project label. These checks do not authenticate the issuer or project of opaque credential bytes and do not prove a live handshake.

No key lookup from environment, argv, files, browser, secret store or alternate project exists. The fixed Development transport has no Production destination fallback. A wrongly sourced credential manually supplied by the operator is not identifiable from the validated string shape.

findings.scope: Actual intended Development credential source, create capability and current validity
findings.facts: Packet credentialSourceReference is UNBOUND; actualCredentialAuthority and securityVerification.adminCredentialAuthority are UNVERIFIED. No provider-issued, independently verifiable non-secret capability record is bound. Prompts, a project label, key syntax, offline fixtures and owner project access do not prove authority.
findings.nextOperatorAction: Owner supplies a sanitized provider-originated record identifying the intended Development credential source/type, exact project and Auth Admin create-user capability, with provenance and custody reference; no key or token value and no credential probe.

findings.scope: Verified source behavior; actual future terminal/process unverified
findings.facts: TTY input is non-echoing, rejects pipes/competing readers and handles cancellation/timeouts; handles redact default JSON/inspection and disposal invalidates retained handles. No module persistence sink exists. Strings/copies cannot be reliably zeroized; spreading/getter reads, HTTP buffers, debugging, heap dumps, transcription and external logging can still expose plaintext.
findings.nextOperatorAction: Before any separately approved credential entry, owner verifies the dedicated local process/TTY has no recording, debugger/preload/body logging and binds that non-secret review; logging clearance must be resolved independently.

findings.scope: Local orchestration checks, not cryptographically authenticated execution authority
findings.facts: The create executor requires a bounded approval object, exact project/run references, three-create ceiling, 120-minute window, <=15-minute remaining wrapper lifetime and fresh exact absence evidence. Option B additionally binds its reviewed run/ledger and freeze. Approval references are caller assertions; the low-level HTTPS transport does not verify an operator approval record or independently establish Admin authority. No automatic live CLI entry point was found.
findings.nextOperatorAction: Owner must review and bind the complete Gate2 execution approval to the exact run/artifacts/limits before invoking the executor; do not substitute the policy-only approval or a fabricated reference string.

findings.scope: No deletion execution is available or authorized through the current Gate2 Admin transport
findings.facts: The transport permits only create POST. No Auth-delete call site was found in the scoped project scripts/application source. The installed SDK has deleteUser, but it is not an A02 delete executor. Gate4 state methods only evaluate exact-ID cleanup/delete evidence; they make no HTTP deletion. Gate4 approval remains UNBOUND.
findings.nextOperatorAction: Keep Auth deletion out of Gate2. Any eventual Gate4 execution must separately bind and review its exact-ID deletion procedure, authority and approval; do not use the presence of an SDK method as permission.

findings.scope: Existing executor/state tooling; not global backend cancellation or cross-process quiescence
findings.facts: The creator is one-shot and stops on uncertain attempts without retry/compensation. Explicit state mode freezes subsequent mutations, rejects repeated in-process run controllers and retains UNKNOWN until reviewed state adoption; adoption grants no retry or cleanup. A new process is not retry authorization.
